title: Atom Adventure (Chemistry)
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the atom — the tiny building block of every element on the periodic table.
meta_desc: GCSE Chemistry Atomic Structure foundations — protons, neutrons, electrons, atomic and mass numbers, isotopes.
final_note: You learned the three subatomic particles, their charges and masses, atomic and mass numbers, and what an isotope is.

concepts.def: Number of protons in the nucleus.
Same element, different number of neutrons.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Every atom is made of protons, neutrons and electrons.

Protons and neutrons sit together in a tiny nucleus. Electrons whizz around it in shells.

Protons are positive, electrons are negative, neutrons are neutral. A neutral atom has the same number of protons and electrons.

The atomic number (Z) is the number of protons. It tells you which element you have. Carbon always has 6 protons.

The mass number (A) is protons + neutrons. So neutrons = A - Z.

Isotopes are atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons.

Carbon-12 and carbon-14 both have 6 protons, but carbon-14 has 2 extra neutrons. They behave the same chemically.

mcqs.q: What does the atomic number tell you?
Where is almost all the mass of an atom located?
options: Electrons contribute significantly to the mass of an atom.
In the nucleus, made up of protons and neutrons.
Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.

mcqs.q: What is different between two isotopes of the same element?
options: Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
Isotopes have different numbers of electrons, which is why their mass differs.
They have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.

mcqs.q: What happens to electrons when sodium reacts with chlorine?
options: Sodium loses one electron to chlorine; the resulting Na+ and Cl- ions attract electrostatically.
Sodium and chlorine share an electron between them.
Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
Protons move from chlorine to sodium to balance the charges.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Mass number”?
options: Same element, different number of neutrons.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Electron”?

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Atomic number”?
options: Number of protons in the nucleus.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Isotope”?
options: Number of protons in the nucleus.
Same element, different number of neutrons.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Proton”?
